Vanessa / Oliver — quick clarifying note: our standard operational model is:

- EU-only policy: customer traffic originates in EU regions and stays there. No non-EU processing unless specifically requested.
- EU-preferred with onshore fallback: primary processing in EU but if an EU pool is unavailable we failover to a customer-designated onshore enclave (if they have a Dedicated / Private deployment) or to an EU-proximate region with contractual safeguards. We do not automatically route to non-EU public regions for customers who require EU residency.

For customers on hosted tier with strict residency requirements we propose a documented fallback: either (a) queued processing until EU capacity available, (b) degraded-mode with local-only outputs, or (c) pop-up Dedicated capacity in EU via an on-demand commit. The choice depends on the customer's risk appetite and contract.

I've amended the routing matrix to add explicit fallback options and trigger thresholds (see column "Fallback trigger / action"). Also added a short note on SCC applicability and our subprocessors catalog.

Marissa — can you confirm the latest subprocessor snapshot (the one with on-prem partner names removed)? Oliver — I can redact partner-hostnames if you want.

Karthik

Oliver — attaching the final packet. Short summary below for Legal: please let us know if you need notarized attestation or a contract amendment referencing the SCCs.

Summary (for EuroBank Legal):
- SCC attestation: Redwood will execute SCCs where required in controller-processor relationships. No deviations from the standard SCC obligations are proposed; exceptions (e.g., customer-specific on-prem integrations) are called out in the attestation appendix.
- Routing & fallback: For customers requiring EU residency, default behavior is EU-only. Where onshore fallback is requested (Dedicated/Private customers), we maintain an EU-managed enclave or capacity pool. Hosted customers without dedicated capacity will not be silently routed to non-EU public regions; fallback options are queued processing, degraded-mode, or customer-approved on-demand Dedicated provisioning.
- DPIA summary: residual risk items include cross-border telemetry for monitoring, ephemeral logs retained for 30 days, and metrics used for autoscaling. Mitigations: aggregated telemetry, strict access controls, KMS-wrapped keys for customer enclaves, and a 30-day retention window for production logs unless otherwise contractually agreed.
